study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Wolfers et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Replicating extensive brain structural heterogeneity in individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study aims to replicate previous findings of extensive individual-level heterogeneity using normative modeling on VBM with GPR in two independent samples. It also explains the purpose of normative modeling (mapping individual deviations) and the broader goal (interpreting group-level findings at the individual level). Both criteria (objectives and purpose of NM) are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Estimating the normative range of voxel-based morphometry (VBM) data among healthy individuals using a Gaussian process regression (GPR) enables us to map individual deviations... Here, we aim to replicate our previous results in two independent samples..."; "These direct replications support that group level-differences... disguise considerable individual differences... with important implications... to the individual with a mental disorder."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility criteria for healthy controls and patients are described (e.g., recruitment source, absence of psychiatric/substance disorders, SCID-based diagnoses for patients). Final sample sizes are reported. However, explicit image quality criteria and reasons for exclusion are not detailed.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Healthy individuals were randomly sampled from national registries and neither they nor their relatives had a psychiatric or alcohol/substance use disorder or cannabis use during the last 3 months."; "Psychiatric diagnosis was established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID)."; "For replication sample 1, we included ... 400 healthy individuals... replication sample 2, ... 312 healthy individuals..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled as covariates in the GPR normative model. The data involve different scanners across discovery and replication, but no explicit site/scanner harmonization or site covariate is described for the normative modeling.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to predict ... from age and sex."; acquisition details list different scanners across samples.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is specified as the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study, with recruitment location, ethics approval, and database selection date mentioned.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study..."; "selected from the TOP-database on the 25th of September 2019."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary data collection details are provided: modality (T1-weighted MRI), scanner make/model, field strength, head coil, and acquisition parameters (TR, TE, FA) for discovery and both replication samples.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "Discovery: ... 1.5 Tesla Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata... TR = 2,730 ms, TE = 3.93 ms, FA = 7... Replication 1: ... 3 Tesla GE 750 Discovery... TR = 8.16 ms, TE = 3.18 ms, FA = 12... Replication 2: ... 3 Tesla GE Signa HDxT... TR = 7.8 ms, TE = 2.956 ms, FA = 12."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described (CAT12/SPM12 VBM; segmentation, normalization, bias correction; 8 mm smoothing; gray matter mask). However, explicit quality control procedures are not described.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "...processed using ... CAT12 ... based on ... SPM12. Images were segmented, normalized, and bias-field-corrected ... all gray and white matter volumes were smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing kernel..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They used 10-fold cross-validation within healthy individuals to estimate out-of-sample performance and report model performance via correlations between predicted and observed values (Figure S1).
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "...estimated the normative range ... in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation..."; "...models performed well ... by plotting the correlation of predicted and observed values under 10-fold cross validation."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study does not apply the trained normative model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals; models are built and validated within the available healthy samples and then applied to patients.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No statement indicating application to an independent external healthy dataset beyond the internal cross-validation.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: GPR normative modeling with covariates age and sex; thresholding of voxelwise Z maps; multiple thresholds explored; PALM for group analysis; software and environment noted (python3.6) with a GitHub link to scripts.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "...estimated the normative model using Gaussian Process Regression (GPR)... from age and sex."; "...thresholded ... at p < .005 (|Z| > 2.6)... also p < .05 and p < .001 ..."; "All analyses were performed in python3.6 ... scripts are available on GitHub (https://github.com/RindKind/)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is assessed using correlations between predicted and observed values under 10-fold cross-validation (reported in Figure S1). Quantitative metrics are referenced but not numerically detailed in the main text.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "...models performed well across the whole brain by plotting the correlation of predicted and observed values under 10-fold cross validation. This is depicted in Figure S1."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: While 10-fold cross-validation is used, the study does not report the sample sizes or demographic characteristics for each partition (training/validation/test).
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: No per-partition sample sizes or demographics provided; only overall sample sizes and use of 10-fold cross-validation are stated.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and versions are stated (python3.6; CAT12/SPM12). Code availability is provided via GitHub. Data availability is described as available upon request due to privacy/ethical restrictions.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "All analyses were performed in python3.6 ... scripts are available on GitHub (https://github.com/RindKind/)."; "The data that support the findings of this study are available on request ... not publicly available due to privacy or ethical restrictions."

Psychiatric diagnosis was established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders (SCID)."; "For replication sample 1, we included 94 ... 116 ..."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Deviation scores are analyzed in relation to clinical symptom severity using PANSS summary scores, satisfying consideration of clinical covariates beyond demographics.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "We tested for associations ... as well as an association with PANSS scores."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort source is the TOP study; recruitment site and catchment area are described, with ethics approval noted.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study ..."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are provided, and clinical characteristics are described via PANSS summary scores. Demographic and clinical information is stated to be summarized in Table 1, though full details are not visible in the text snippet.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "Table 1 summarizes the demographic and clinical information..."; PANSS summary table lines are present (e.g., "PANSS total (mean ± std) ...").

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures include SCID for diagnosis and PANSS for symptom assessment; assessment was conducted by trained clinicians.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "Patients were assessed by trained physicians or clinical psychologists. Psychiatric diagnosis was established using ... SCID. Symptoms were assessed using PANSS."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The meaning of deviation scores is defined via voxel-wise Z-scores (predicted-observed normalized by predictive uncertainty). Thresholds for defining extreme deviations are specified (|Z|>2.6, with sensitivity checks at 1.96 and 3.1). Clinical implications are explored via associations with diagnosis and PANSS, and discussion emphasizes individual-level heterogeneity versus group findings.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "...computing a Z-score for each voxel reflecting the difference between the predicted and the observed gray matter volume normalized by the uncertainty of the prediction..."; "...thresholded ... at p < .005 (i.e., |Z| > 2.6)... also ... p < .05 (|Z| > 1.96) and p < .001 (|Z| > 3.1) ... associations with PANSS scores."
